> Clunkey Rover is a small autonomous robot designed to explore robotics, embedded electronics, mechanical engineering, and CAD. The robot will use an ESP32 as its main controller, two geared motors for movement, and an ultrasonic distance sensor to detect objects in front of it. When the robot detects an obstacle, it will stop, turn, and continue moving in a different direction. I will design the robot's chassis in CAD, including the motor mounts, sensor mount, electronics platform, and battery compartment. I want the design to be compact, functional, and easy to modify as I learn more about the hardware. This project is inspired by my experience on a FIRST Robotics team and my interest in mechanical engineering and robotics. The name Clunkey Rover is inspired by Clunkey, a robotics mascot that became meaningful to my team. I want this project to be a way to continue building and experimenting with robotics while learning how mechanical parts, electronics, sensors, and programming work together in one complete system.

## Design

### 2026-10-01 — Clunkey Rover — Warm-Up Session 1

**4h**

Clunkey Rover — Warm-Up Session 1

Today I worked on the initial design and planning for my Clunkey Rover, a mini autonomous robot inspired by my experience with FIRST Robotics and my interest in mechanical engineering and robotics.

I created a public GitHub repository and organized it into sections for CAD, electronics, firmware, and my journal. I also created a concept sketch to plan the rover's overall design, chassis, sensor placement, electronics, and battery location. My planned robot will use an ESP32, geared motors, an ultrasonic distance sensor, and a battery.

I do not have the physical parts yet, so I focused on the design and planning stage instead of building. This session helped me think about how the different mechanical and electrical parts will work together. My next step is to develop the CAD design further, determine the exact parts I need, and eventually build and test the rover.

### 2026-10-04 — Today I continued working on the Clunkey Rover design and planning. I organized the Bill of Materials with the planned components, quantities, estimated costs, and purposes, keeping the project within

**6h**

Today I continued working on the Clunkey Rover design and planning. I organized the Bill of Materials with the planned components, quantities, estimated costs, and purposes, keeping the project within the Hack Club Tier 2 budget. I also worked on the electronics design by planning how the ESP32, motor drivers, four motors, ultrasonic sensor, and battery system will work together. Finally, I continued developing the CAD design plan for the four-wheel chassis, including motor mounting locations, electronics placement, battery placement, and the front ultrasonic sensor mount. These plans will help guide the physical build once the parts are available.

### 2026-10-04 — Today I continued developing the Clunkey Rover by creating and refining the 3D CAD chassis design, documenting the planned electronics system, and creating a firmware flowchart for the rover’s autonom

**7h**

Today I continued developing the Clunkey Rover by creating and refining the 3D CAD chassis design, documenting the planned electronics system, and creating a firmware flowchart for the rover’s autonomous behavior. I worked on the four-wheel-drive chassis layout in Onshape, including the wheel and motor positions, electronics area, battery area, and front sensor location. I also documented how the ESP32, two TB6612FNG motor drivers, four geared motors, HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor, and battery system will work together. Finally, I created a firmware flowchart showing how the rover is planned to move, detect obstacles, stop, turn, and continue. These designs are still part of the planning stage and will be refined during the physical build and testing.
